units.description: The number of lines in s. A line ends at a line feed (byte 10) and includes it; a final piece with no line feed also counts as a line. The empty text has 0 lines. Carriage returns and any other bytes are ordinary. Never panics.

units.signature: fn cdiff_same_line[&ra, &rb](a: &ra [byte], a0: int, a1: int, b: &rb [byte], b0: int, b1: int) -> [] bool
units.description: True exactly when the byte range a[a0..a1] and the byte range b[b0..b1] have the same length and the same bytes, in order. An empty range equals an empty range. Two lines are the same only when every byte, including a final line feed, is the same. Never panics: ranges are within the texts when called.
tests: pub fn test_same_line_1() -> [] int { test.assert(cdiff_same_line("abc", 0, 3, "abc", 0, 3) == true); return 0; }
pub fn test_same_line_2() -> [] int { test.assert(cdiff_same_line("a\n", 0, 2, "a", 0, 1) == false); return 0; }
pub fn test_same_line_3() -> [] int { test.assert(cdiff_same_line("ab", 0, 1, "ab", 1, 2) == false); return 0; }

units.signature: fn cdiff_range[&h](heap: &!h Heap, start: int, count: int) -> [heap] buffer.Buffer
units.description: The text of a hunk range: start alone when count is 1, otherwise start, a comma and count (so 0 gives "start,0"). Written as decimal digits; use buffer.push_nat for the numbers. Import std.buffer. Returns a new buffer.
tests: fn cases_range_same[&a, &b](x: &a [byte], y: &b [byte]) -> [] bool { if len(x) != len(y) { return false; } var i = 0; while i < len(x) { if int_of(x[i]) != int_of(y[i]) { return false; } i = i + 1; } return true; }

fn cases_range_is[&h, &w](heap: &!h Heap, a1: int, a2: int, want: &w [byte]) -> [heap] int { let got = cdiff_range(heap, a1, a2); var same = false; borrow got as &x in { same = cases_range_same(buffer.bytes(x), want); } buffer.drop(heap, got); if same { return 0; } return 1; }

units.signature: fn cdiff_script[&h, &ra, &rb](heap: &!h Heap, a: &ra [byte], b: &rb [byte]) -> [heap] Box[[byte]]
units.description: The line edit script from a to b, as one byte per line of the merged result, in order: a space for a line in both texts, '-' for a line only in a, '+' for a line only in b. The number of non-space bytes must be the smallest possible (a shortest edit script over whole lines, computed with a line-by-line dynamic-programming table or Myers' algorithm; exponential search is not allowed, and it must be fast on several thousand lines each). Within a run of changes, the '-' bytes come before the '+' bytes. The empty pair gives an empty box. Free the box yourself where it is used. Use cdiff_lines, cdiff_line_end and cdiff_same_line for the lines.

units.signature: fn unified[&h, &rn, &rm, &ra, &rb](heap: &!h Heap, a_name: &rn [byte], b_name: &rm [byte], a: &ra [byte], b: &rb [byte], context: int) -> [heap] buffer.Buffer
units.description: The unified diff of a and b in the format GNU diff -u prints. First the line "--- " then a_name then a line feed, then "+++ " then b_name then a line feed (names exactly as given). Then one hunk per group of changes, from cdiff_script: a header "@@ -OLD +NEW @@" and a line feed, where OLD and NEW are written with cdiff_range (start of the first line of the range, 1-based; a range with count 0 uses the number of the line before it, so an insertion into an empty a is -0,0). Each hunk line is a space, '-' or '+' followed by the line itself. A line with no final line feed is followed by a line feed and "\ No newline at end of file" and a line feed, for context, '-' and '+' lines alike. Up to context unchanged lines before and after each group of changes, fewer at the ends (a negative context counts as 0). Two groups are in one hunk when the unchanged lines between them are at most 2 * context; otherwise separate hunks. Hunks in order, not overlapping. When a and b are the same text the result is the empty text. A line counted for a hunk is numbered from 1 in a and in b. Import std.buffer and use cdiff_range for the numbers.

units.signature: fn apply[&h, &rp, &ra](heap: &!h Heap, patch: &rp [byte], a: &ra [byte]) -> [heap] result.Result[buffer.Buffer, int]
units.description: Apply a unified diff in the format of unified to a and give the new text, or an error number. An empty patch gives a unchanged. Otherwise the patch begins with a line starting "--- " and a line starting "+++ " (any names), then hunks with a header that must be exactly "@@ -S[,C] +T[,D] @@" followed by a line feed (a count of 1 may be written without it; numbers have at most 9 digits). A hunk's first old line is line S of a (line S+1 when C is 0). Numbers are exact: no search and no fuzz. Every context line and every '-' line must match a's line byte for byte, including whether it has a final line feed; the result is a with the '-' lines removed and the '+' lines added. The numbers after '+' are used only for their counts. A "\ No newline at end of file" line after a line marks that line as having no line feed. Hunks must be in order and not overlap. The patch is read from the top and the first fault decides: Err(1) when the patch is malformed (a missing "--- " or "+++ " line, a header not of that form, a hunk line whose first byte is not a space, '-' or '+', a hunk with fewer or more lines than its counts, hunks out of order); Err(2) when the patch is well formed but does not fit a (a context or '-' line differs, or a hunk begins after the end of a). Never panics on any bytes. Import std.buffer and std.result.

apply(heap, "--- a/f
+++ b/f
@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@
 a
-b
+B
 c
", "a
b
c
") == result.Result::Ok("a
B
c
")
